main_text.l: V. Circuli, quos oportet in Sphæra mundi,
hoc est, tum in cœlo, tum in terra imaginari,
sunt numero octo. Ex his sunt quatuor maiores, qui
mundum diuidunt in duas partes æquales; vt horizon,
meridianus, æquator, & Zodiacus: & totidem minores,
qui mundum diuidunt in duas partes inæquales; vt tro-
picus cancri & capricorni, polaris arcticus & antarcticus.
Quod attinet ad duos coluros, vnum solstitiorum, alte-
rum æqui noctiorum, illi locum duntaxat habent in cœ-
lo. Ex his circulis horiζon visibilem cœli & terræ partem
ab inuisibili dirimit: meridianus inter ortum & occasum
est medius, ita vt respondeat puncto verticali: æquator in-
ter duos mundi polos, siue inter septentrionem & meri-
diem, est medius: Zodiacus obliquè secat æquatorem,
duosque tropicos attingit: tropicus cancri in superiori,
capricorni, in inferiori parte Zodiacum contingit: polaris ar-
cticus circuit polum superiorem, antarcticus, inferiorem.
Hos circulos oportet partim mente concipere, partim
delineare. Mente concipiendi sunt partim in cœlo
& in
terra, partim in museo, partim in compasso, partim de-
nique in solario. Delineandi sunt in globo cœlesti & ter-
restri, in Sphæra pertusa siue armillari, in mappis siue ta-
bulis geographicis tum vniuersalibus, tum particulari-
bus; denique in compasso & solario maioribus.
XIII.
I. Vranoscopia sacra complectitur duas so-
lum partes: videlicet Sphæricam, & Cō-
putum. Nihil enim ex sacris potest colligi, quod illu-
stret Theoriam planetarum, & Astrologiam, quæ sunt
duæ reliquæ partes Vranoscopiæ.

page.notes: The Greek zeta in "horiζon" is printed as a Greek letter in the Latin word; kept as printed. The punctum sign after "puncto" is a small circle, transcribed as the word "puncto". The text is cut off at the bottom, so the second paragraph ends at "Sphæ-" on this part. The page number is printed as "3" followed by a mark that could be a damaged "0"; it is read as 30 with [?]. The marginal number beside "quæ sunt" is read as 35 and is uncertain. The "I." and "II." are numbered paragraph openings and are kept as text.
